summary: Barcelona Light, Westfield, NY: 1829 fieldstone tower, lit by natural gas from 1831; discontinued 1859; New York State historic site, grounds open.

structures.note: enlarged and dormers added in the 1880s

access.note: Grounds open year-round; keeper's cottage open in staffed hours; tower closed (LighthouseFriends) or weather-dependent (Park Finder).

facts.agency: New York State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (state historic site)

Fieldstone tower and keeper's dwelling finished by June 1829 (contract let August 1828)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The historical society gives 2007 and LighthouseFriends gives 2008 for the State's acquisition. The story states both.

LighthouseFriends names Wilhelm Willink, Wilhelm Willink the younger and Cornelius Vallenhoven as sellers; the historical society says the Holland Land Company. Both agree on 10 July 1828 and $50. The story states both.
The 1851 Treasury passage, as LighthouseFriends quotes it, puts the gas pipe at two miles. The story gives that figure as the Treasury's.
The USLHS record gives 1829 as the original lens year, which matches the 11 lamps and reflectors. LighthouseFriends records a fourth-order Fresnel lens fitted in 1857.

notes_for_editor: (1) Almost every fact comes from LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased, one short quotation per sentence). The NRHP nomination for 72000825 is not digitized on NPGallery (76-character placeholder), so the NRHP listing date rests on LighthouseFriends and the historical society. (2) The USCG Historian's archived page for Barcelona Harbor Light could not be read (Wayback captures return the calendar page only; the 2024 capture is 403). (3) The corpus has no Barcelona hits in the Lighthouse Board (1891-1901), Commissioner (1915-22) or Bulletin (1912-39) volumes. The Lighthouse Board's 1855 and 1859 reports, and the Treasury's 1851 report, are quoted only through LighthouseFriends; not verified against primary text. (4) Newspaper search for 'carbureted hydrogen' and 'Portland' in 1831-1840 found nothing; the Fredonia Censor was not located. (5) The Life-Saving Service annual reports list 'Barcelona Harbor, Lake Erie, N.Y.' as a locality with counts in tables for 1879-1884; the tables were not read in full, so no wreck or rescue is recorded here. (6) Tourism sites say the light was 'the first lighthouse in the world' lit by natural gas. The story does not repeat that claim; the historical society and LighthouseFriends say first public building in the United States. (7) Park Finder's hours are a third-party listing of NY State Parks' published schedule; check the official NY State Parks page before a visit. (8) The record's lens is null; the story gives the 1857 fourth-order lens from LighthouseFriends. (9) Lane's appointment quotation is LighthouseFriends' quotation of an unnamed description; the original was not found. (10) The Wikipedia article was read for leads only and is not cited. (11) Storm date: LighthouseFriends calls the 1844 storm the Great Gale; the historical society calls it the 'Great Storm' of 15 October 1844. The story treats them as one storm, which the two sources' wording supports but neither states outright. (12) Gas: the story and record now say the tower was lit by oil lamps from 1829 and by natural gas from the 1 January 1831 contract; the earlier record note 'lit with natural gas, then oil' misdated the gas. (13) The historical society gives the lot seller as the Holland Land Company and LighthouseFriends names three men; both are stated in the story.
